report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of gated_writes.py: _PinnedWorktreeGit, _hardened_env, _read_gitdir_pointer, _reattempt, _as_cancel_predicate, _CumulativeGateCancelled, _promote_one_inner. Verified docstring claims against code and identified risks.
risks: _promote_one_inner | high | git apply is run with --whitespace=nowarn, not --check; the comment claims a passing apply proves nothing about semantic correctness, but the code proceeds to commit and run the full test suite on the applied patch. The staleness check only compares base_revision to current_head, not whether the patch still applies cleanly. A failed apply is handled, but a successful apply with semantic breakage is not detected until the cumulative gate runs; if no test_command is configured, the commit is made without any verification. This risk is inherent to the design (regeneration on staleness) but worth noting: the comment's claim that 'git apply --check would only prove bytes still match' is true, but the code does not even run --check; it directly applies. The claimed safety net is the cumulative gate, which is optional. | Confirm whether the cumulative gate is always required or if test_command can be None in production; if None, the commit is unverified.

_promote_one_inner | medium | The cumulative gate's RunnerContext is constructed with task_id='kairos-cumulative-gate' and instruction='cumulative re-gate', but the test_command is split with shlex.split and passed to command_gate. The command_gate is not defined in this chunk; its behavior regarding cancellation and timeout is uncheckable. The comment claims it is cancellable, but the actual implementation is elsewhere. | Inspect command_gate to verify it honors is_cancelled and timeout_s.

_PinnedWorktreeGit.run | medium | The git command is run with cwd=str(self.worktree) and --git-dir/--work-tree flags. However, the _hardened_env() function strips GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE from the environment, but the --git-dir and --work-tree flags are passed explicitly. If the worktree path contains special characters (e.g., spaces), they are not quoted; subprocess.run with a list does not need quoting, but the path is used as part of the flag value, which is fine. The risk is that the admin_dir is read once at construction, but if the worktree is moved or the .git file changes after construction, the pointer is stale. The class docstring explicitly says to construct after create_worktree and before git apply, so this is by design. | No action needed; the risk is mitigated by the documented contract.

_hardened_env | low | The environment is copied from os.environ, but the function does not remove GIT_CONFIG_COUNT or GIT_CONFIG_KEY_* variables, which can also be used to inject config. The _GIT_EXEC_CONFIG list adds -c options, but does not clear GIT_CONFIG_COUNT. This could allow a candidate to set GIT_CONFIG_COUNT via the environment if the parent process has it. However, the function does pop GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, so it is mostly hardened. | Check if GIT_CONFIG_COUNT is a real risk; if so, add it to the pop list.

_promote_one_inner | medium | The code raises a RuntimeError if test_cwd is not None, '', or '.'. This is a hard refusal with no repair path in this chunk. The docstring/comment says the cumulative re-gate needs test_cwd='.', but the project may configure a different test_cwd. This could be a legitimate configuration error, but the error message is not actionable. | Confirm whether the project always uses test_cwd='.'; if not, the code will fail on valid configurations.

handoff.purpose: Contains git hardening, worktree pinning, candidate regeneration, cancel token normalization, and the cumulative re-gate promotion logic.

symbols.name: _GIT_EXEC_CONFIG
symbols.note: Tuple of git -c key=value strings to disable external hooks, credential helpers, and protocol extensions.

symbols.name: _hardened_env
symbols.note: Returns a copy of os.environ with git config/attribute system files disabled and leaky git variables removed.

symbols.name: _read_gitdir_pointer
symbols.note: Reads a worktree's .git pointer (either a directory or a gitdir: file) and returns the admin dir path, or None.

symbols.name: _PinnedWorktreeGit
symbols.note: Pins git calls to a worktree's admin dir captured at construction to avoid candidate-controlled .git file rewrites.

symbols.name: _PinnedWorktreeGit.__init__
symbols.note: Stores worktree path and captures admin_dir via _read_gitdir_pointer.

symbols.name: _PinnedWorktreeGit.run
symbols.note: Runs a git command with pinned --git-dir/--work-tree and hardened config/env; raises RuntimeError on non-zero exit if check=True.

symbols.name: _reattempt
symbols.note: Re-runs a candidate's TaskSpec against a new base revision via run_attempt, returning a fresh GatedCandidate.

symbols.name: _as_cancel_predicate
symbols.note: Normalizes a cancel token (None, callable, or is_set-bearing object) into a zero-arg predicate that swallows exceptions.

symbols.name: _CumulativeGateCancelled
symbols.note: Exception type raised when the cumulative re-gate is cancelled, to distinguish cancellation from gate failure.

symbols.name: _promote_one_inner
symbols.note: Promotes a single candidate: checks staleness, optionally regenerates, applies patch, commits, and runs cumulative gate.

observations.what: The cumulative gate is only run if test_command is truthy; if test_command is None, the commit is made without any verification after the patch is applied.

The staleness check compares artifact.base_revision to current_head, but the regeneration uses _reattempt which may produce a new artifact with a different base_revision; the recursive call then re-checks staleness. This is correct but could lead to infinite recursion if the base keeps moving; the _retried flag bounds it to one retry.

The cumulative gate's RunnerContext is constructed with task_id='kairos-cumulative-gate' and instruction='cumulative re-gate', but the test_command is split with shlex.split and passed to command_gate. The command_gate is not defined in this chunk; its behavior regarding cancellation and timeout is uncheckable.

The _hardened_env function does not remove GIT_CONFIG_COUNT or GIT_CONFIG_KEY_* variables, which could be used to inject git config. However, the _GIT_EXEC_CONFIG list adds -c options that override some settings, but GIT_CONFIG_COUNT could still be used.

The _read_gitdir_pointer reads the .git file with errors='replace', which could mask encoding issues; if the file is binary or corrupt, it may return a wrong path. However, the function returns None if the text does not start with 'gitdir:', so it is mostly safe.
The _promote_one_inner raises a RuntimeError if test_cwd is not '.', but the error message is not actionable; it does not suggest a repair. This is a refusal with no reachable repair in this chunk.
